title: When the Smile Burns
premise: Sable Eastwick takes a teaching post at Hollowmere's village school, where a classroom of children vanished in 1911 and a new one disappears every winter since. The villagers' relentless warmth—the casseroles, the invitations, the smiles—turns out to be a mechanism: the town must welcome a stranger each frost season, or the frost takes their own children instead. When Sable realizes the ringing of the melted bell marks the choosing, he must decide whether to expose the truth and shatter the village, or accept the invitation meant for him. He survives by turning the ritual inside out—refusing the welcome while naming the children of 1911 aloud—freeing the village at the cost of his belonging, and he leaves at sunrise as the frost writes a final pattern on his window: a child's handprint, waving goodbye.
about_author: Mirabel Ravensworth is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent nine years in villages where everyone knew everyone, and one winter where she began to suspect that was the problem. She writes horror about the violence of belonging from a house with excellent locks.

chapters.title: The Warmest Welcome
chapters.summary: Sable arrives in Hollowmere to teach its eleven remaining pupils; the villagers greet him with unsettling, uniform enthusiasm, and headmistress Mrs. Alder insists he sign a ledger dated 1911. His skeptical POV establishes the school, the missing-class rumor he dismisses as superstition. Emotional beat: uneasy comfort—he wants to belong and doesn't trust wanting it.

chapters.title: Eleven Names, Twelve Desks
chapters.summary: In Sable's POV, he counts twelve desks for eleven children and finds a class photo from 1911 where one face is scratched out. A pupil, Wren, quietly tells him the twelfth desk is 'for the one the frost picks.' Emotional beat: the first crack in his rationalism, masked by professional briskness.

chapters.title: The Bell That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Sable, awake at 3 a.m., hears the church bell ring though the archive confirms it was melted in 1911. Villagers the next morning all heard nothing—or claim to. His POV tightens with paranoia as Mrs. Alder gently suggests he stay in after dark. Emotional beat: gaslit isolation deepening into dread.

chapters.title: Frost Patterns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV: the children know the rules—don't answer the bell, don't accept a gift after dark, don't let a stranger's smile be the last thing you see. Wren decides Sable is kind and tries to protect him, breaking a rule herself. Emotional beat: tenderness as transgression; the reader learns the mechanics before the teacher does.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Sable finds the 1911 ledger: the village invited something in to save their harvest, and it has taken a child each winter since—unless given a stranger. His POV shifts from disbelief to horrified comprehension. Emotional beat: the sickening click of a puzzle whose answer he was always part of.

chapters.title: Casserole Season
chapters.summary: The village's warmth becomes predatory—gifts left at his door, invitations he must refuse, neighbors watching his windows. Sable realizes every kindness is a snare and every refusal insults them. His POV. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth—the village isn't evil, it's terrified, and that's worse.

chapters.title: Wren Is Missing
chapters.summary: Wren doesn't come to school; the frost on her window forms a bell shape. Sable confronts the village, who mourn her with practiced, rehearsed grief—and he understands they gave her up because he refused to leave. His POV, guilt and fury. Emotional beat: the cost of his skepticism lands on a child.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: The bell rings at midnight and doesn't stop. Sable follows the sound to the frozen churchyard where the frost is writing names—1911's vanished class, and now Wren's. Mrs. Alder, revealed as a 1911 survivor, begs him to accept the invitation and end it. His POV. Emotional beat: climax of temptation—belonging offered as surrender.

chapters.title: Refusal, Spoken Plainly
chapters.summary: Sable breaks the ritual by naming the 1911 children aloud, one by one, refusing the welcome without fleeing—forcing the frost-thing to be witnessed rather than invited. The bell cracks mid-peal; the names lift off the ground like breath. Wren walks out of the churchyard, frost-burned but alive. His POV. Emotional beat: truth as weapon, spoken at terrible volume.

chapters.title: Sunrise, and the Handprint
chapters.summary: Dawn: the village is freed but cannot forgive the man who unmade its bargain, and Sable cannot forgive them. He packs; Wren alone says goodbye. On his frost-covered window, a small handprint waves. His POV, closing with Wren watching the road. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—he saved them by never belonging, and the frost, respectfully, remembers him.
